history.period: Founded 1599; burnt 1632; present church built c.1660–1661; declared a minor basilica 25 November 1988
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Basilica of the Holy Rosary, commonly Bandel Church, is a Roman Catholic (Archdiocese of Calcutta) church and one of the oldest Christian places of worship in Bengal. Portuguese settlers, with permission from Akbar c.1571 and full preaching rights via Captain Pedro Tavares, built it in 1599 with Augustinian friars; it was burnt in the 1632 sack of Hooghly and rebuilt by John Comes/Gomez de Soto c.1660–1661, the original 1599 keystone being preserved in the monastery gate. Dedicated to Nossa Senhora do Rosário (Our Lady of the Rosary); Pope John Paul II declared it a minor basilica on 25 November 1988 (WB Tourism gives 24 November — minor discrepancy). Notable: the ship's mast at the church front, offered by a Portuguese captain rescued from a Bay of Bengal storm. FLAGS: (1) NON-HINDU record — Roman Catholic church, not a Hindu temple; (2) CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Hooghly' — actual state is West Bengal; (3) CSV town 'Hooghly' corrected to actual town Bandel.

name: Bandel Church
town_description: Bandel is a port town on the Hooghly river in Hooghly district, West Bengal — its name derives from the Bengali word 'bandar' meaning port; the Portuguese used it as a port from the mid-16th century, and the church and monastery are the remaining relics of that settlement.

travel.railway: Bandel Junction on the Howrah–Bardhaman main line; Howrah/Katwa/Memari/Burdwan locals halt here; Bandel–Naihati local and ferry link to Naihati
